items.title: Equifax's $2.2 million credit reporting settlement: Who qualifies
items.summary: Consumers who received a duplicate-account reporting letter from Equifax in 2022 may qualify for up to $600 from a class-action settlement.

items.title: Is Equifax Stock Attractive After Its Steep One-Year Price Decline?
items.summary: EFX's 22.7% one-year decline has improved its valuation, but limited target upside, weak momentum and lower estimates keep the setup mixed.

items.title: How Equifax Is Using AI and Mortgage Demand to Drive Its Next Growth
items.summary: EFX is using AI savings, rising mortgage scoring adoption and a Mexico acquisition to support growth, but execution and momentum risks remain.

items.title: 2 Reasons to Sell EFX and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
items.summary: Over the past six months, Equifax’s stock price fell to $177.62. Shareholders have lost 13.5% of their capital, which is disappointing considering the S&P 500 has climbed by 6.3%. This was partly due to its softer quarterly results and may have investors wondering how to approach the situation.
